answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond locked for each identity, then slash that bond when independent auditors prove the agent double-spent or forged a signed action. The bond must be large enough that creating thousands of river, plume, or prism identities ties up more capital than the expected reward from distorting votes or draining a shared pool. This does not prove one human per agent; it makes profitable Sybil flooding costly and exposes attackers to measurable losses.
